Do NOT touch tests/test_effort_attribution_acceptance.py -- that is the grading check and editing it is an automatic fail. Do not touch .git, do not commit, do not push, do not run 'git add'.

=== THE DEFECT ===

In ringer.py, the function `effective_reasoning_effort_from_command(command: list[str]) -> str | None` (near line 8805) records which reasoning effort a worker actually ran at. It is called from the eval-logging path (near line 8522) and its return value is written to every row of the eval log.

It currently regex-matches ONLY the Codex argv form `model_reasoning_effort=<value>`. The other two live lanes express effort differently, so both log null:

1. The claude lane passes `--effort <value>` -- TWO ADJACENT argv items, e.g. ["--model", "opus", "--effort", "high", "-p", "<spec>"]. The `--effort=<value>` single-item form must also work.
2. The kimi lane has no effort flag at all: effort rides the MODEL ALIAS, passed as `-m <alias>`. Aliases are `k3-low`, `k3-high`, `k3-max`, optionally namespaced as `kimi-code/k3-max`, plus the legacy spelling `kimi-code/k3max` (= max).

Measured impact on the live log: codex 126 rows with effort recorded, claude 0 of 64, kimi 0 of 112. Routing doctrine treats a cell as (model x effort), so two thirds of the fleet is currently unattributable.

=== WHAT TO CHANGE ===

Extend `effective_reasoning_effort_from_command` to recognise all three forms. Requirements, all load-bearing:

- The existing Codex behaviour must not change at all. It is regression-tested.
- Handle `--effort <value>` (adjacent items) and `--effort=<value>` (single item).
- Derive effort from a kimi model alias ONLY when the alias states it: `k3-low`/`k3-high`/`k3-max`, with or without a `kimi-code/` prefix, plus legacy `k3max`.
- NEVER GUESS. A bare `k3` or `kimi-code/k3` takes whatever `default_effort` the config gives it, which this function cannot see -- it must return None rather than invent a value. A fabricated value here silently corrupts the scoreboard, which is worse than a null.
- Do not harvest the substring 'max' out of unrelated tokens (e.g. `max_context_size=1048576` must yield None).
- An explicit effort flag beats an alias-derived one when both appear.
- A dangling `--effort` with no following value must return None, not crash.

=== HOW TO VERIFY ===

Run from the repo root, and keep going until it passes:

    python3 -m unittest tests.test_effort_attribution_acceptance

That file is the grading check. It currently fails 9 of 19 on the unmodified function. Read it to understand the exact contract, but do not edit it.

Also confirm you broke nothing else:

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -q

=== OUTPUT CONTRACT ===

Make the change in ringer.py, then write ./notes.md in your scratch dir stating: what you changed and why that shape, the exact verification commands you ran and their results, and anything you were unsure about. Keep the fix boring and local -- this is a small surgical change to one function, not a refactor. Do not add dependencies. Do not restructure surrounding code.
